Our approach to obtaining a contradiction relies on the overlap of input lengths on which all of the algorithms A1 , . . . , Ak succeed in their respective inversions. The negation of this assumption only implies the existence of infinitely-often one-way functions. Given that we only get infinitely-often security anyway, we are able to weaken our assumption to L∈ / P/poly instead of needing L ∈ / ioP/poly as in our other results. 4 One-Way Functions We complete our transformation by extending the result of [7] that shows that assuming there are zero-knowledge arguments for NP, auxiliary-input one-way functions imply standard one-way functions. We follow the approach taken by [4] in the context of weak zero-knowledge arguments, showing that the auxiliary-input OWFs obtained in the previous sections also imply standard one-way functions.
